claims.excerpt: The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people and the number of employed people—not everyone who does not have a job.
claims.claim: The rate’s denominator combines employed and unemployed people, rather than including everyone without a job.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: The unemployment rate divides unemployed people by the sum of employed and unemployed people.
claims.narrative: Establish that the unemployment rate divides unemployed people by the combined number of employed and unemployed people, rather than by everyone without a job.
claims.explanation: The piece accurately describes the denominator and distinguishes it from everyone without a job.
claims.materiality: Material to explaining who is included in the rate.

claims.excerpt: someone whose only job-search activity was browsing job listings has not met the active-search requirement.
claims.claim: Browsing job listings as the only job-search activity does not meet the active-search requirement.
claims.label: F2 material incorrect, unsupported or misleading
claims.evidence: Passive-only job search does not count as active search.
claims.narrative: someone whose only job-search activity was browsing listings. The first may qualify without an active search; passive browsing alone does not meet the active-search requirement.
claims.explanation: The source says passive-only search is insufficient but does not establish that browsing job listings is necessarily passive-only. The piece turns that unsupported example into a definite classification; the same specificity appears in the upstream idea and narrative.
claims.materiality: Material because this is one of the piece’s central contrasting examples.
